## Example 5.7 · (b) Decay {#ss5-example-5-7-b .gp-lesson}

b) For the GP $b_n=48\left(\dfrac12\right)^{n-1}$ $(0<r<1)$:

::: {.gp-subparts}
i) Evaluate the first four terms.

ii) Describe what happens to the value of $b_n$ as $n\to\infty$.
:::

<p class="booklet-cue">Booklet p. 33 · Example 5.7(b)</p>

::: notes

(i) 48,24,12,6. (ii) b_n tends to 0 from above as n increases without bound, but no finite-index term is zero. A continuous generating function is f(x)=48(1/2)^(x−1)=96(1/2)^x. The question concerns a term limit, not an infinite series sum. Geometric series and their sums come later. The graph slide's Decay preset illustrates this sequence.

:::
